subject: Request: Temporary rate-window & burst mitigation for holiday promo
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@greenleafcpg.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@greenleafcpg.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Unexpected spike — can we get a temporary rate window?

Hi Priyom,

Quick one — our holiday bundle launches next Monday and we're already seeing significant traffic spikes in the test environment. The calls are being throttled at our current rate cap and the storefront response times are starting to degrade. We have a short window (Nov 22–28) where we expect 5–8x normal peak QPS.

Can Redwood provide a temporary easing of the burst/fairness policy (or an alternative like a prioritized rate-window) for that week? We're happy to accept a temporary higher spend commitment or short-term reserved capacity if that helps.

Attaching a small sample of the traffic logs.

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Engineering, Greenleaf CPG
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@greenleafcpg.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike — can we get a temporary rate window?

Maya — thanks for the heads up and for the log sample. I copied Lauren (sales lead) and Rafael (runtime) so we can move quickly. A couple of options we commonly use:

- Short-term prioritized rate window: carve out a time-bounded policy that routes Greenleaf traffic to a slightly higher priority queue with a temporary soft cap increase.
- Temporary reserved tokens: short-term monthly commit for the promo week (prorated) to guarantee throughput and avoid fairness throttles.
- Canary routing to a dedicated pool: if you want near-zero throttling we can put a small dedicated pool behind a canary route for the week, but that has a fixed cost and requires quick sign-off.

Can you confirm: 1) expected peak QPS (rough estimate), 2) budget flex for the week (range), 3) whether the promo is global or limited to a region? Rafael — any constraints or lead time from the runtime side to open a prioritized window for Nov 22?

I'll draft a short mutual action plan once we have those numbers.

— Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@greenleafcpg.com>, procurement@greenleafcpg.com
Date: 2026-11-19T08:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike — can we get a temporary rate window?

Quick note from pricing — we can do a time-limited uplift with two commercial paths:

1) Pro-rated reserved capacity for one week: ~1.1x of the estimated peak cost (fastest to enable, invoice on next cycle).
2) Temporary priority window + overage pricing: keep base plan active, increase token cap for the window and bill incremental at a higher rate (capped).

If Greenleaf confirms a relaxed cap for 6 days, we can offer a one-time credit in lieu of a larger minimum if the week doesn't materialize to the forecasted usage.

Rafael — any runtime notes? What lead time do you need to change policy and create a prioritized route?

— Lauren
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@greenleafcpg.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike — can we get a temporary rate window?

On Fri, Nov 19, 2026 at 08:25, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai wrote:
> Quick note from pricing — we can do a time-limited uplift with two commercial paths:
>
> 1) Pro-rated reserved capacity for one week...

Maya / team — engineering can enable a prioritized rate window with the following constraints:

- Lead time: 24 hours to provision the routing policy and validate KV cache warm-up.
- Fairness: the prioritized queue will bypass standard fairness throttles but is limited to a configurable burst budget (we recommend 7x baseline for safety).
- Monitoring: we'll enable a temporary dashboard and alerting; Redwood will run a short smoke test before cutover.
- Fallback: automatic rollback to baseline policy if latency degradation or error rate crosses thresholds.

Action items (proposed MAP):
1) Greenleaf to confirm expected peak QPS and approved budget by EOD Nov 21.
2) Redwood to provision prioritized window on Nov 21 PST and run validation.
3) Cutover Nov 22 00:00 PST → Nov 28 23:59 PST.
4) Post-week cost reconciliation and (if applicable) one-time credit applied within 30 days.

Attaching a short MAP PDF and the spike CSV you sent for the record.

— Rafael
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
